flashcard_questions.q: What is introduced into the body during vaccination?
flashcard_questions.a: A small quantity of a dead or inactive form of the pathogen.

flashcard_questions.q: Why can a vaccine not give a person the disease?
flashcard_questions.a: The pathogen in it is dead or inactive, but still carries the same antigens.

flashcard_questions.q: What do memory lymphocytes do if the same pathogen enters the body again?
flashcard_questions.a: They trigger a much faster and stronger antibody response.

flashcard_questions.q: What is meant by herd immunity in a population?
flashcard_questions.a: So many people are immune that the pathogen cannot find enough hosts to spread.

flashcard_questions.q: Which disease was completely eradicated by global vaccination by 1980?
Why can antibiotics not kill viruses?
flashcard_questions.a: Viruses reproduce inside human cells, so destroying them would destroy the body's own cells.

flashcard_questions.q: What do painkillers do for a person with an infection?
flashcard_questions.a: They treat the symptoms, such as pain and fever, but kill no pathogens.

flashcard_questions.q: How does an antibiotic-resistant strain of bacteria arise?
flashcard_questions.a: A mutation in the bacterial DNA lets some bacteria survive the antibiotic and reproduce.

flashcard_questions.q: Why must a patient finish the whole course of antibiotics?
flashcard_questions.a: So every bacterium is killed and none survives to develop resistance.

flashcard_questions.q: Which heart drug originally came from foxgloves?
Which painkiller originally came from willow bark?
Who discovered penicillin in 1928 from the Penicillium mould?
What happens during the preclinical testing of a new drug?
flashcard_questions.a: It is tested on cells and tissues first, then on live animals.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a placebo used for in a double blind trial?
flashcard_questions.a: It looks like the drug but has no active ingredient, so bias is removed.

flashcard_questions.q: What must happen to trial results before they are published?
flashcard_questions.a: They must pass peer review, which is scrutiny by other scientists.
